questions.text: उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसमें 325 लघुबीजाणुमातृकोशिकाओं के लघुबीजाणुजनन विभाजन के परिणामस्वरूप निर्मित होने वाले परागकणों की सही संख्या को दर्शाया गया है।
questions.text_english: Choose the option that gives the correct number of pollen grains that will be formed after 325 microspore mother cells undergo microsporogenesis.
questions.solution: Each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis (microsporogenesis) to produce 4 microspores (pollen grains). Therefore, 325 microspore mother cells will produce 325 × 4 = 1300 pollen grains. Options A (325) and B (650) are wrong because they do not account for tetrad formation during meiosis. Option D (975) has no biological basis.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रत्येक लघुबीजाणुमातृकोशिका अर्धसूत्री विभाजन (लघुबीजाणुजनन) के द्वारा 4 लघुबीजाणु (परागकण) उत्पन्न करती है। अतः 325 × 4 = 1300 परागकण बनते हैं।

questions.text: आर्तव चक्र की उस प्रावस्था का चयन कीजिए जिसमें ग्राफी पुटक (ग्राफियन फॉलिकल) का शेष बचा हुआ भाग पीत पिंड (कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम) में परिवर्तित हो जाता है।
questions.text_english: Select the phase of menstrual cycle in which the remaining parts of Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum.
questions.solution: After ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle transforms into a temporary endocrine structure called the corpus luteum during the secretory (luteal) phase. The corpus luteum secretes progesterone, which prepares the endometrium for implantation. The ovulatory phase is when the follicle ruptures; proliferative phase involves follicle growth; menstrual phase involves shedding of the uterine lining.
questions.solution_hindi: अंडोत्सर्ग के बाद, स्रावी (ल्यूटियल) प्रावस्था में ग्राफी पुटक का शेष भाग पीत पिंड (कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम) में परिवर्तित हो जाता है जो प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करता है।

questions.text: एक स्त्री की अंड/डिंबवाहिनी (फैलोपियन नलिका) अवरुद्ध है और उसका आईवीएफ उपचार चल रहा है। जिस तकनीक द्वारा 8 ब्लास्टोमियर से अधिक कोशिकाओं वाले भ्रूण को परिवहन हेतु स्थानांतरित किया जाएगा, वह है:
questions.text_english: A female undergoing IVF treatment has blocked fallopian tube. The technique by which the embryo with more than 8 blastomeres will be transferred into the female for further development is:
questions.solution: IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer) is the technique used to transfer embryos with more than 8 blastomeres directly into the uterus for further development. ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) is used only for zygote or early cleavage embryos and requires a patent fallopian tube, which is blocked in this case. GIFT involves transferring gametes, and AI is artificial insemination, not applicable here.
questions.solution_hindi: IUT (इंट्रा यूटेराइन ट्रांसफर) तकनीक में 8 ब्लास्टोमियर से अधिक कोशिकाओं वाले भ्रूण को सीधे गर्भाशय में स्थानांतरित किया जाता है। चूंकि फैलोपियन नलिका अवरुद्ध है, इसलिए ZIFT का उपयोग नहीं किया जा सकता।

questions.text: सही कथन का चयन कीजिए। किसी एक गुणसूत्र (क्रोमोसोम) पर अवस्थित सभी जीन:
questions.text_english: Select the correct statement. All genes located on the same chromosome:

options.A: उनके बीच पारस्परिक दूरी (सापेक्ष दूरी) के आधार पर विभिन्न समूह बनाते हैं।
options.D: पारस्परिक/अन्योन्यक्रिया वाले समूह बनाते हैं जो दृश्यप्ररूप (फीनोटाइप) को प्रभावित करता है।

options_english.A: form different groups depending upon their relative distance.
options_english.D: form interactive groups that affect the phenotype.

questions.solution: All genes located on the same chromosome form one linkage group because they tend to be inherited together during meiosis. The number of linkage groups in an organism equals its haploid chromosome number. Option A is incorrect because relative distance determines the degree of linkage, not separate groups. Options C and D are biologically incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: एक ही गुणसूत्र पर स्थित सभी जीन एक सहलग्नता समूह (linkage group) बनाते हैं, क्योंकि अर्धसूत्री विभाजन के दौरान वे एक साथ वंशागत होते हैं।

questions.text:
सही कथनों का चयन कीजिए:
(i) बहुसिस्ट्रॉनिक (पॉलीसिस्ट्रॉनिक) एमआरएनए सामान्यतः सुकेन्द्रकियों में पाया जाता है।
(ii) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज II एमआरएनए के पूर्ववर्ती, एचएनआरएनए (hnRNA) का अनुलेखन करता है।
(iii) जब दूत-आरएनए (एमआरएनए) राइबोसोम की बड़ी उपएकक के साथ एकीकृत होता है तब एमआरएनए का स्थानांतरण (रूपांतरण) प्रक्रम प्रारंभ होता है।
(iv) रोध प्रकूट (स्टॉप कोडॉन) में कोई टी-आरएनए नहीं होता है।
questions.text_english:
Choose the correct statements:
(i) Polycistronic mRNA is generally found in eukaryotes.
(ii) The RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor of mRNA, the hnRNA.
(iii) The process of translation of mRNA begins when the mRNA encounters the large subunit of ribosomes.
(iv) Stop codons do not have any tRNAs.
questions.solution: Statement (ii) is correct — RNA polymerase II transcribes the hnRNA (heterogeneous nuclear RNA), which is the precursor of mRNA in eukaryotes. Statement (iv) is correct — stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) do not have corresponding tRNAs; instead, release factors recognize them and terminate translation. Statement (i) is wrong because polycistronic mRNA is found in prokaryotes, not eukaryotes. Statement (iii) is wrong because translation begins when mRNA associates with the small subunit of ribosome, not the large subunit.
questions.solution_hindi: कथन (ii) सही है — RNA पॉलीमरेज II द्वारा hnRNA का अनुलेखन होता है। कथन (iv) सही है — स्टॉप कोडॉन के लिए कोई tRNA नहीं होता। कथन (i) गलत है — पॉलीसिस्ट्रॉनिक mRNA प्रोकैरियोट में पाया जाता है। कथन (iii) गलत है — अनुवाद mRNA के छोटी उपएकक से जुड़ने पर शुरू होता है।

questions.text: मानव के विलुप्त पूर्वज का नाम बताइए जो केवल फल खाते थे तथा पत्थर के हथियारों से शिकार करते थे।
questions.text_english: Name the extinct ancestor of humans who ate only fruits and hunted with stone weapons.
questions.solution: Australopithecus was an extinct human ancestor who was fruit-eating and also used stone tools to hunt small animals. They walked erect and lived in East Africa. Dryopithecus were more ape-like and did not use stone tools. Ramapithecus was more like apes. Homo erectus had a larger brain and more advanced tool use, going beyond simple stone hunting weapons.
questions.solution_hindi: ऑस्ट्रेलोपिथेकस वह विलुप्त पूर्वज थे जो केवल फल खाते थे और पत्थर के हथियारों से शिकार करते थे। वे सीधे खड़े होकर चलते थे और पूर्वी अफ्रीका में रहते थे।

questions.text:
निकोटीन रक्तचाप (दाब) तथा हृदय स्पंदन दर को प्रभावित करता है जिसका कारण कुछ विशिष्ट अधिवृक्क हॉर्मोनों का मोचन (स्रावण) होना है। कुछ अधिवृक्क हॉर्मोन निम्नलिखित हैं:
(i) ऐड्रिनेलीन
(ii) कॉर्टिसोल
(iii) नॉर-ऐड्रिनेलीन
(iv) ऐल्डोस्टेरोन
सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english:
Nicotine affects blood pressure and heart rate due to release of certain adrenal hormones. Following are some of the adrenal hormones:
(i) Adrenaline
(ii) Cortisol
(iii) Noradrenaline
(iv) Aldosterone
Select the correct option:
questions.solution: Nicotine stimulates the adrenal medulla to release adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine). These catecholamine hormones directly increase heart rate and blood pressure — adrenaline by increasing heart rate and cardiac output, and noradrenaline by causing vasoconstriction. Cortisol and aldosterone are secreted by the adrenal cortex and are not directly stimulated by nicotine to affect heart rate.
questions.solution_hindi: निकोटीन अधिवृक्क मेड्यूला को ऐड्रिनेलीन और नॉर-ऐड्रिनेलीन स्रावित करने के लिए उत्तेजित करता है, जो हृदय स्पंदन दर और रक्तचाप को बढ़ाते हैं।

questions.text: पीड़क तितली के लार्वा (कैटरपिलर) के जैव नियंत्रण हेतु उपयोग किया जाने वाला सूक्ष्मजीव है:
questions.text_english: Microbes used for biocontrol of pest butterfly caterpillars is:
questions.solution: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is the bacterium used as a biocontrol agent against pest butterfly and moth caterpillars. It produces crystalline insecticidal proteins (Cry proteins) that are toxic to the gut of the caterpillars. Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a yeast used in fermentation. Trichoderma is a fungal biocontrol agent against plant pathogens. Streptococcus is not used for biocontrol.
questions.solution_hindi: बैसिलस थ्यूरिंजिएंसिस (Bt) एक जीवाणु है जो तितली के लार्वा (कैटरपिलर) के जैव नियंत्रण के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। यह Cry प्रोटीन उत्पन्न करता है जो कीट की आंत में विषाक्त होते हैं।

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए आरेखों में दो विभिन्न स्तनधारियों के कपाल (खोपड़ियों) को दर्शाया गया है। निम्नलिखित विकल्पों में से कौन-सा इन दोनों खोपड़ियों के बीच ठीक विभेद करता है?
questions.text_english: The given diagram shows the skulls of two different mammals. Which of the following options accurately describes the differences between these skulls?

options.A: खोपड़ी B खोपड़ी A का पूर्वज है।
options.B: खोपड़ी A की मस्तिष्क धारिता खोपड़ी B से अधिक है।
options.C: खोपड़ी A एक मानव की तथा खोपड़ी B एक वयस्क चिम्पैंजी की है।
options.D: खोपड़ी A एक वयस्क चिम्पैंजी की तथा खोपड़ी B एक मानव की है।

options_english.A: Skull B is the ancestor of skull A.
options_english.B: Skull A has more brain capacity than skull B.
options_english.C: Skull A is of a human and skull B is of an adult chimpanzee.
options_english.D: Skull A is of an adult chimpanzee and skull B is of a human.

questions.solution: Skull A shows a prognathous face (projecting jaw), smaller cranial vault, and pronounced brow ridges — features characteristic of an adult chimpanzee. Skull B has a large, rounded cranium, flat face, and reduced jaw — features of a modern human. Option B is wrong because the human skull (B) has more brain capacity. Chimpanzees are not ancestors of modern humans; they are our closest living relatives, so option A is incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: खोपड़ी A में आगे निकला हुआ जबड़ा और छोटी कपाल गुहा होती है जो चिम्पैंजी की विशेषता है। खोपड़ी B में बड़ी गोल कपाल गुहा है जो मानव की विशेषता है।

questions.text: आरएनएआई में, निम्नलिखित जैवअणुओं में से किसका उपयोग जीनों को निष्क्रिय (शमन) करने में किया जाता है?
questions.text_english: In RNAi, genes are silenced using which of the following biomolecules?
questions.solution: RNA interference (RNAi) is a gene silencing mechanism in which double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) complementary to the target mRNA is introduced into the cell. The dsRNA is processed by the enzyme Dicer into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), which then bind to and degrade the target mRNA, silencing the gene. Single-stranded DNA, double-stranded DNA, and single-stranded RNA are not the molecules used in the RNAi pathway.
questions.solution_hindi: आरएनएआई (RNAi) में द्विसूत्री आरएनए (dsRNA) का उपयोग जीनों को निष्क्रिय करने के लिए किया जाता है। यह एंजाइम Dicer द्वारा siRNA में परिवर्तित होकर लक्ष्य mRNA को अपघटित करता है।

questions.text: कॉनेल के परिष्कृत क्षेत्र के प्रयोगों में पाया गया कि स्कॉटलैंड के चट्टानी समुद्र तटों पर बड़े बार्नेकल बैलेनस का अंतरज्वारीय क्षेत्र में प्रभुत्व था तथा इसने छोटे बार्नेकल चैथेमेलस को उस क्षेत्र से बाहर निकाल दिया। इसका कारण था:
questions.text_english: Connell's elegant field experiments on the rocky seacoast of Scotland, found that larger barnacles Balanus dominated the intertidal area and removed the smaller barnacles Chathamalus. This happened due to:
questions.solution: Connell's classic experiment is a textbook example of interspecific competition. The larger barnacle Balanus physically displaced the smaller Chathamalus by outcompeting it for space in the intertidal zone. This is competition, not parasitism (where one organism lives on or in another), not predation (where one organism eats another), and not mutualism (where both organisms benefit).
questions.solution_hindi: कॉनेल का प्रयोग अंतरजातीय स्पर्धा (interspecific competition) का उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है। बड़े बार्नेकल बैलेनस ने स्थान के लिए स्पर्धा करके छोटे चैथेमेलस को बाहर कर दिया।

questions.text: जीन क्राई-I एबी द्वारा प्रकूटित प्रोटीन निम्नलिखित में से किसका संक्रमण (ग्रसन) बाधित करती है?
questions.text_english: Protein encoded by gene Cry-I Ab controls the infestation of which of the following?
questions.solution: The Cry-I Ab protein, encoded by the Cry-I Ab gene from Bacillus thuringiensis, is specifically toxic to corn borers (stem borer of maize). The Bt maize has been engineered with this gene to provide resistance. Cry-I Ac controls cotton bollworms. Mosquitoes are controlled by Cry-II Ab. Agrobacterium is not a pest but a bacterium used in plant transformation.
questions.solution_hindi: Cry-I Ab जीन द्वारा प्रकूटित प्रोटीन मक्का छेदक (corn borer) के संक्रमण को बाधित करती है। Bt मक्का में यह जीन डाला गया है। कपास गोलक शलभ को Cry-I Ac नियंत्रित करता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): अननुमील्य परागणी पुष्प सुनिश्चित रूप से बीज उत्पन्न करते हैं।
कारण (R): अननुमील्य परागणी पुष्प सदैव स्वयुग्मकी होते हैं तथा परागण हेतु किसी परागणकर्ता पर निर्भर नहीं करते।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers have assured seed set.
Reason (R): Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous and do not depend on any pollinating agents.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Cleistogamous flowers never open, which means pollination occurs within the closed flower (autogamy). Since they do not require any external pollinating agent, self-pollination is guaranteed, and consequently seed set is always assured. The reason accurately explains why seed set is certain — the flowers are invariably autogamous and independent of pollinators.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। अननुमील्य पुष्प कभी नहीं खुलते, इसलिए वे सदैव स्वयुग्मकी होते हैं और परागणकर्ता पर निर्भर नहीं करते, जिससे बीज उत्पादन सुनिश्चित रहता है।

कारण (R): मानव रुधिर वर्ग विशेषक के लिए जीन तीन युग्मविकल्पी (ऐलीलिक) स्वरूपों यथा IA, IB तथा i के रूप में विद्यमान होते हैं।

questions.text_english: How do 'implants' act as an effective method of contraception in human females? Mention one advantage of implants over contraceptive pills.

questions.solution: Implants are small hormone-releasing devices inserted under the skin (subcutaneous) of the upper arm. They slowly and continuously release progestin hormones into the bloodstream, which prevent ovulation, thicken cervical mucus to block sperm, and thin the uterine lining to prevent implantation. This makes them an effective contraceptive method. One important advantage of implants over contraceptive pills is that implants provide long-term, continuous contraception lasting 3 to 5 years without requiring the woman to remember to take a pill every day, thus reducing the chance of user error.

questions.solution: Apomictic seeds can be developed through nucellar polyembryony, where diploid nucellar cells of the ovule develop into embryos without fertilization, producing seeds genetically identical to the parent plant. Farmers prefer apomictic seeds over hybrid seeds because apomictic seeds maintain hybrid vigour (heterosis) uniformly in every generation. With hybrid seeds, vigour diminishes in subsequent generations and farmers must purchase fresh hybrid seeds each year. Apomictic seeds allow farmers to save seeds from one harvest and use them in the next season without any loss of yield quality.

key_points: ori (origin of replication): Controls the replication of recombinant DNA within the host cell and determines the copy number of the vector.
Restriction site: The site where restriction enzymes cut the vector to allow insertion of foreign DNA (e.g., EcoRI site in ampicillin resistance gene, HindIII in tetracycline resistance gene).

questions.solution: The 'ori' (origin of replication) in pBR322 is the specific DNA sequence from which replication of the plasmid begins inside the host cell. It controls the copy number of the vector — i.e., how many copies of the plasmid are maintained per cell. The restriction site is a specific recognition sequence where restriction endonucleases cut the vector DNA to create a linear form, allowing the foreign DNA fragment (gene of interest) to be inserted. In pBR322, restriction sites are located within the antibiotic resistance genes (ampR and tetR), enabling insertional inactivation to identify recombinants.

questions.solution: Two important ecosystem services are: first, purification of air and water — forests and wetlands filter pollutants from water, and plants absorb carbon dioxide while releasing oxygen, maintaining air quality; second, nutrient cycling — decomposers break down dead organic matter and recycle essential minerals like nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon back into the soil and atmosphere, maintaining soil fertility for plant growth. questions.text_english: Differentiate between wind-pollinated and insect-pollinated flowers. Give an example of each type.

questions.solution: Wind-pollinated flowers are generally small and inconspicuous with dull colours. They do not produce nectar or fragrance. Their pollen grains are produced in very large quantities, are light, smooth, and non-sticky so they can be easily carried by wind. The stigmas are feathery or large to catch airborne pollen. Example: Maize (Zea mays). Insect-pollinated flowers, on the other hand, are large and brightly coloured with attractive petals to lure insects. They produce nectar and fragrance. Their pollen is sticky or spiny to adhere to the body of insects. The stigmas are also sticky to hold the pollen carried by insects. Example: China rose (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis).

questions.text_english:

key_points: (a) The complete transcription unit: 3'-Promoter - ATGCATGCATAG (coding strand, 5'→3') - Terminator-5'. The template strand runs 3'→5' opposite to the coding strand.
(b) The RNA strand transcribed (from template strand 3'→5') will be: 5'-UAUGCAUGCAUAG-3'. This mRNA runs 5'→3' and is complementary to the template strand (not the coding strand).

questions.solution: The coding strand given is: 5' — A T G C A T G C A T A G — 3'. The template strand (anti-sense strand) runs antiparallel: 3' — T A C G T A C G T A T C — 5'. To construct the complete transcription unit, the promoter is added upstream (to the 3' end of the template strand, i.e., towards the left of the coding strand), and the terminator sequence is added downstream (to the 5' end of template strand, i.e., to the right end of coding strand). The RNA polymerase reads the template strand from 3'→5' and synthesises the RNA strand in 5'→3' direction. The transcribed RNA strand is: 5' — U A U G C A U G C A U A G — 3'. Its polarity is 5'→3', running in the same direction as the coding strand, and it is complementary to the template strand.
questions.solution_hindi: कोडिंग रज्जु: 5'-ATGCATGCATAG-3'। टेम्पलेट रज्जु: 3'-TACGTACGTATC-5'। अनुलेखन इकाई में उन्नायक (promoter) को टेम्पलेट रज्जु के 3' सिरे की ओर और समापक (terminator) को 5' सिरे की ओर जोड़ते हैं। अभिलेखित RNA: 5'-UAUGCAUGCAUAG-3' (ध्रुवणता: 5'→3')।

questions.text: ऐसे तीन विभिन्न तरीकों की व्याख्या कीजिए जिनमें प्राकृतिक वरण परिचालित होता है। ग्राफीय आरेखों की सहायता से इसकी व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the three different ways in which natural selection operates. Explain with the help of graphs.

key_points: Stabilising selection: Favours the average phenotype, reducing variation; the bell curve becomes narrower.
Directional selection: Shifts the mean of a trait in one direction, favouring one extreme phenotype; the bell curve shifts left or right.
Disruptive (Diversifying) selection: Favours both extreme phenotypes and eliminates the average; the bell curve splits into two peaks.

questions.image_description: Three bell-curve graphs showing: (1) Stabilising selection — original broad bell curve narrows. (2) Directional selection — bell curve shifts to the right (or left). (3) Disruptive selection — single bell curve splits into two separate peaks at either extreme.
questions.solution: Natural selection operates in three distinct ways. First, stabilising selection occurs when the environment favours individuals with the average (intermediate) phenotype and eliminates those at both extremes. This reduces variation and maintains the population near the mean — shown graphically as a narrowing of the bell curve. Second, directional selection occurs when environmental conditions change so that one extreme phenotype is favoured over the other. Over time, the entire bell curve shifts in one direction. Industrial melanism in peppered moths is a classic example. Third, disruptive (diversifying) selection favours both extreme phenotypes while selecting against the intermediate. This results in the bell curve splitting into two peaks, potentially leading to speciation over time.
questions.solution_hindi: प्राकृतिक वरण तीन प्रकार से क्रियाशील होता है: (1) स्थिरीकारक वरण — मध्यवर्ती लक्षणप्ररूप का पक्ष लेता है, विचरण कम करता है। (2) दिशात्मक वरण — एक चरम लक्षणप्ररूप को लाभ मिलता है, माध्य एक दिशा में स्थानांतरित होता है। (3) विघटनकारी वरण — दोनों चरम लक्षणप्ररूपों को लाभ मिलता है, मध्यवर्ती का चयन नहीं होता।

questions.text_english:
(a) How do some viruses cause cancer in humans?
(b) How do benign tumours turn malignant? How do malignant tumours harm the human body?

key_points: (a) Oncogenic viruses carry genes called oncogenes (viral oncogenes/v-onc), which when integrated into the host cell genome activate cellular oncogenes (proto-oncogenes), causing uncontrolled cell division.
(b) Benign tumour cells become malignant through metastasis — they break away, invade surrounding tissues, enter blood/lymph and spread to distant organs, damaging normal tissue and organ function.

questions.solution: Some viruses called oncogenic viruses carry specific genes known as viral oncogenes (v-onc). When these viruses infect a host cell, they integrate their genetic material into the host genome. The viral oncogenes activate cellular proto-oncogenes (c-onc), transforming them into oncogenes that stimulate uncontrolled cell proliferation, leading to tumour formation. Examples include Human Papillomavirus (HPV) causing cervical cancer. Benign tumours have cells that remain confined to their original location and do not spread. They become malignant when tumour cells acquire the ability to migrate — this property is called metastasis. Malignant cells detach from the primary tumour, invade surrounding tissues, enter blood vessels or lymphatics, and spread to distant organs. Malignant tumours harm the body by destroying normal tissues and organs, competing with healthy cells for nutrients, and causing organ failure.
questions.solution_hindi: ऑन्कोजेनिक वायरस अपने v-onc जीन परपोषी जीनोम में समेकित कर देते हैं, जो proto-oncogene को सक्रिय कर असामान्य कोशिका विभाजन प्रेरित करते हैं। सुदम अर्बुद की कोशिकाएं मेटास्टेसिस द्वारा दुर्दम बनती हैं — वे प्राथमिक स्थान से अलग होकर रक्त/लसीका द्वारा दूरस्थ अंगों तक फैलती हैं और सामान्य ऊतकों को नष्ट करती हैं।

questions.text:
(क) इंसुलिन प्रोइंसुलिन से किस प्रकार विलग (भिन्न) है?
(ख) आरडीएनए प्रौद्योगिकी द्वारा मानव इंसुलिन के निर्मित होने की तकनीक के सभी चरणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) How is insulin different from proinsulin?
(b) Explain all the stages of how human insulin is produced through rDNA technology.

key_points: (a) Proinsulin has an extra C-peptide chain connecting the A and B chains, making it a single polypeptide. Mature insulin lacks the C-peptide — it consists of only A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds.

(b) rDNA insulin production: genes for A and B chains synthesised separately → inserted into pBR322 plasmid → E. coli expression → separate A and B chains extracted → combined with disulfide bonds formed → active human insulin.

questions.solution: Proinsulin is the inactive precursor of insulin that contains three polypeptide chains — A, B, and C — connected together. During maturation, the C-peptide is removed by specific proteases, and the remaining A and B chains are joined by disulfide bonds to form the active insulin molecule. Thus, insulin differs from proinsulin in lacking the C-peptide chain. For rDNA technology: The DNA sequences coding for the A and B chains of human insulin were chemically synthesised. Each sequence was separately inserted into a plasmid vector (pBR322) and introduced into E. coli. The bacterium expressed the genes, producing the A and B polypeptide chains separately. The chains were then extracted and combined in vitro under conditions that allow disulfide bonds to form between them, yielding biologically active human insulin. This method was developed by Eli Lilly company and the insulin produced is known as Humulin.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रोइंसुलिन में A, B और C तीनों पेप्टाइड श्रृंखलाएं होती हैं। परिपक्व इंसुलिन में C-पेप्टाइड हटा दिया जाता है और A व B श्रृंखलाएं डाइसल्फाइड बंध से जुड़ी होती हैं। rDNA तकनीक: A और B श्रृंखलाओं के जीन रासायनिक रूप से संश्लेषित → pBR322 में डाले → E. coli में अभिव्यक्त → अलग-अलग श्रृंखलाएं निकालकर डाइसल्फाइड बंध से जोड़ी → सक्रिय इंसुलिन प्राप्त।

questions.text_english:
(a) Study the graph given below and answer the questions that follow:
(i) Write the status of food and space in the curves a and b.
(ii) In the absence of predators, which one of the two curves would appropriately depict the prey population?
(iii) 'Time' has been shown on x-axis and there is a parallel dotted line above it. Give the significance of this dotted line.
OR
(b) Answer the following questions:
(i) Define 'predation'.
(ii) Why is predation required in a community of different organisms? Give any two points.
(iii) Why are predators 'prudent' in nature?

key_points: (a)(i) Curve a — food and space are unlimited (J-shaped, exponential growth). Curve b — food and space are limited (S-shaped, logistic growth).
(a)(ii) In the absence of predators, curve a (exponential/J-shaped) would depict prey population growth.
(a)(iii) The dotted line represents the carrying capacity (K) — the maximum population size that the environment can support.
(b)(i) Predation is an interspecific interaction where one organism (predator) captures and feeds on another organism (prey).
(b)(ii) Predation transfers energy between trophic levels; it keeps prey population in check preventing overgrazing.
(b)(iii) Predators are prudent because they never completely exterminate prey — if prey were eliminated, predators themselves would starve.

questions.solution: For part (a): Curve a represents exponential (J-shaped) growth, where food and space are unlimited — the population grows without any restriction. Curve b represents logistic (S-shaped) growth, where food and space are limited — the population grows initially but levels off as resources become scarce. In the absence of predators, the prey population would show curve a (exponential growth) because there is no mortality from predation. The dotted line parallel to the x-axis represents the carrying capacity (K), which is the maximum number of individuals an environment can support given the available resources. The population stabilises at K in logistic growth. For part (b OR): Predation is an interspecific interaction in which one organism (predator) hunts and kills another organism (prey) for food. Predation is necessary in a community because it transfers energy across trophic levels, maintaining energy flow, and it keeps prey populations in check, preventing overexploitation of plant resources and maintaining ecological balance. Predators are described as prudent because they never over-hunt their prey — if they did, they would eliminate their own food source and starve. Natural selection has thus favoured predators that regulate their feeding to ensure prey populations survive.
questions.solution_hindi: वक्र a — जहाँ आहार और स्थान असीमित हैं, जनसंख्या J-आकार (घातांकीय) वृद्धि दर्शाती है। वक्र b — सीमित संसाधन, S-आकार (लॉजिस्टिक) वृद्धि। परभक्षियों की अनुपस्थिति में वक्र a शिकार समष्टि को दर्शाएगा। बिंदुरेखा = वहन क्षमता (K)। परभक्षण: एक जीव दूसरे को पकड़कर खाता है; यह ऊर्जा स्थानांतरण करता है और शिकार समष्टि को नियंत्रित रखता है। परभक्षी विवेकी होते हैं क्योंकि वे कभी अपने शिकार को पूर्णतः नष्ट नहीं करते।

(क) इस केस (उदाहरण) में किस प्रकार की जैव-विविधता का संरक्षण परिलक्षित होता है?
(ख) ऐसे कोई दो अन्य उपायों की व्याख्या कीजिए जो इस प्रकार के संरक्षण में सहायक हैं।
(ग) प्राणि (जन्तु) उद्यानों के अतिरिक्त, एक अन्य स्थान का उल्लेख कीजिए जिसका उपयोग इस उद्देश्य से किया जा रहा है।
questions.text_english:
There are many animals, which have become extinct in the wild, but continue to be maintained in zoological parks. Answer the questions that follow:
(a) What type of bio-diversity conservation is observed in this case?
(b) Explain any other two ways which help in this type of conservation.
(c) Besides zoological parks, mention one place that serves this purpose.

key_points: (a) Ex-situ conservation — conservation outside the natural habitat.
(b) Two other ways: cryopreservation of gametes/seeds/embryos in gene banks; maintenance of tissue culture banks for plant species.
(c) Botanical gardens / seed banks (e.g., National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources).

questions.solution: When animals that are extinct in the wild are maintained in zoological parks, this is called ex-situ conservation — conservation of species outside their natural habitat. Two other important methods of ex-situ conservation are: first, cryopreservation, where gametes, seeds, or embryos of endangered species are preserved at very low temperatures (in liquid nitrogen) in gene banks, keeping them viable for long periods; second, in vitro fertilization and embryo banking, where embryos of threatened species are stored and can be used for future breeding programmes. Besides zoological parks, botanical gardens also serve the purpose of ex-situ conservation for plant species, maintaining living collections of threatened plant species.
questions.solution_hindi: प्राणि उद्यान में रखे जाने वाले जीवों का बाह्य-स्थाने (ex-situ) संरक्षण होता है — जीवों का उनके प्राकृतिक आवास से बाहर संरक्षण। दो अन्य उपाय: (1) क्रायोसंरक्षण — युग्मक, बीज या भ्रूण को तरल नाइट्रोजन में संरक्षित करना। (2) इन विट्रो निषेचन और भ्रूण बैंकिंग। प्राणि उद्यान के अतिरिक्त वानस्पतिक उद्यान (botanical gardens) इस उद्देश्य की पूर्ति करते हैं।

एक कोशिकीय तंत्र में जीन प्रोटीन/एंजाइम के रूप में अभिव्यक्त होता है। कोशिका तंत्र में जीन की अभिव्यक्ति किस प्रकार होती है, इसकी आवश्यकता कब होती है तथा जीन की अभिव्यक्ति का नियमन किस प्रकार होता है? — असीमकेन्द्रकी कोशिका तंत्र में यह समझने के लिए एक आनुवंशिकीविज्ञ फ्रांस्वा जैकब तथा एक जैवरसायनविज्ञ जैक्स मोनोड ने संयुक्त रूप से प्रयास किए। ई. कोलाई में किए गए लैक्टोज उपापचय पर किए गए उनके प्रयोगों के लिए तथा 'लैक प्रचालेक' (लैक ऑपेरॉन) की संकल्पना प्रस्तुत करने के लिए उन्हें 1965 में नोबेल पुरस्कार से सम्मानित किया गया।
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
Gene expresses itself in a cell system as a protein/enzyme. How an expression of gene occurs in a cell system, when it needs to occur and how the gene expression is regulated in prokaryotic cell system was studied by the combined efforts of Francois Jacob, a geneticist and Jacques Monod, a biochemist. For their work on lactose metabolism in E. coli and introducing the concept of 'lac operon', they were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1965.

sub_questions.text: यह कहा गया कि बैक्टीरियल (जीवाणु) कोशिका में 'लैक ऑपेरॉन' बहुत ही कम (अल्प) स्तर पर सदा ही क्रियाशील रहता है। कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: It is said that 'lac operon' has to be operational at a very low level in the bacterial cell all the time. Justify.

key_points: The lac operon must remain functional at a basal level to allow a small amount of beta-galactosidase to be present so that when lactose enters the cell, it can be converted to allolactose (the true inducer), which then removes the repressor and fully induces the operon.

sub_questions.solution: The lac operon must remain operational at a very low (basal) level at all times because a small amount of the enzyme beta-galactosidase is always needed. When lactose enters the bacterial cell, this small quantity of beta-galactosidase converts it into allolactose, which is the actual inducer. Allolactose then binds to the repressor protein and inactivates it, allowing full transcription of the structural genes. If the operon were completely switched off, no allolactose could be formed and the operon could never be induced.

sub_questions.text:
ई. कोलाई के लैक ऑपेरॉन में संरचनात्मक जीन किस प्रकार सक्रिय होते हैं?
अथवा
इस प्रचालेक (ऑपेरॉन) का नियमन ऋणात्मक नियमन (निगेटिव रेगुलेशन) क्यों कहलाता है?
sub_questions.text_english:
How are the structural genes activated in the lac operon in E. coli?
OR
Why is the regulation of operon called negative regulation?

key_points: Structural genes (lacZ, lacY, lacA) are activated when allolactose (inducer) binds to the repressor protein, causing it to detach from the operator, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe the structural genes. / It is called negative regulation because normally the repressor protein keeps the operon turned off (negative control); gene expression only occurs when the repressor is inactivated.

sub_questions.solution: In E. coli, the structural genes lacZ, lacY, and lacA of the lac operon are normally switched off because a repressor protein (encoded by the regulator gene i) binds to the operator region, blocking RNA polymerase. When lactose is present, allolactose (a metabolite of lactose) acts as an inducer and binds to the repressor protein. This changes the repressor's shape, causing it to detach from the operator. RNA polymerase is then free to move along the DNA and transcribe all three structural genes together as a single polycistronic mRNA. The regulation is called negative regulation because the default state of the operon is 'off' — the repressor protein negatively controls expression by blocking transcription unless the inducer removes it.

sub_questions.text: लैक ऑपेरॉन को अनुलेखनीय नियमित तंत्र क्यों कहा जाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is lac operon said to be a transcriptionally regulated system?

key_points: Lac operon is transcriptionally regulated because the control of gene expression occurs at the level of transcription — the repressor protein controls whether RNA polymerase can transcribe the structural genes or not, not at the level of translation or post-translation.

sub_questions.solution: The lac operon is called a transcriptionally regulated system because the entire regulatory mechanism operates at the level of transcription — the first step of gene expression. The repressor protein controls gene expression by binding to or detaching from the operator, which directly determines whether RNA polymerase can initiate transcription of the structural genes (lacZ, lacY, lacA). When the repressor is bound to the operator, transcription is blocked. When allolactose removes the repressor, transcription proceeds. Since the primary control point is transcription itself (not translation or post-translational modification), the lac operon is rightly called a transcriptionally regulated system.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
Immunity in our body is of two types (i) Innate immunity, and (ii) Acquired immunity. Innate immunity is a non-specific defence mechanism, whereas Acquired immunity is pathogen specific. Acquired immunity is characterised by memory. Antibodies are specific to antigens and there are four types of antibodies produced in our body — IgA, IgE, IgG and IgM. It shows primary response where it encounters the pathogen for the first time and secondary response during the subsequent encounters with the same antigen/pathogen. These immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in the blood.

sub_questions.text_english: Name the two types of specialised cells which carry out the primary and secondary responses.

key_points: B lymphocytes (B cells) — produce antibodies for humoral immune response. T lymphocytes (T cells) — mediate cell-mediated immunity.

sub_questions.solution: The two types of specialised lymphocytes that carry out primary and secondary immune responses are B lymphocytes (B cells) and T lymphocytes (T cells). B lymphocytes are responsible for the humoral immune response — they differentiate into plasma cells that produce antibodies against specific antigens. T lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity and also include memory T cells that mount a faster, stronger secondary response upon re-exposure to the same antigen.

sub_questions.text_english:
Name any two barriers present in our body that provide innate immunity.
OR
The organ transplants (grafts) are often rejected if not taken from suitable compatible persons. Mention the characteristic of our immune system that is responsible for the rejection.

key_points: Two barriers: Skin (physical/mechanical barrier) and mucus secreted by epithelial lining of respiratory/gastrointestinal tracts. / For OR: The immune system's ability to distinguish 'self' from 'non-self' (MHC-based recognition) is responsible for graft rejection.

sub_questions.solution: Two barriers providing innate immunity are the skin, which acts as a physical barrier preventing entry of pathogens, and the mucus secreted by the epithelial cells lining the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts, which traps pathogens and prevents them from entering the body. (For OR: Organ transplants are rejected because the immune system can recognise the transplanted organ as 'non-self'. This is due to the presence of Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules, also known as Human Leukocyte Antigens (HLA) in humans, on the surface of cells. If the donor's MHC profile does not match the recipient's, the immune system mounts a response against the graft and destroys it.)

sub_questions.text: सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा (ऐक्टिव इम्युनिटी) निष्क्रिय (पैसिव इम्युनिटी) से किस प्रकार भिन्न है? कोई दो अंतर लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How is active immunity different from passive immunity? Write any two differences.

key_points: Active immunity: generated by the individual's own immune system in response to antigen exposure; long-lasting with immunological memory.
Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies transferred from outside (e.g., mother to foetus via placenta, or antiserum injection); no memory, short-lived protection.

sub_questions.solution: Active immunity is produced when the individual's own immune system responds to an antigen (pathogen or vaccine) by producing antibodies and memory cells. It takes time to develop but is long-lasting because of immunological memory — the body responds faster and stronger upon re-exposure. Passive immunity, on the other hand, involves the transfer of ready-made antibodies into an individual from an external source — for example, IgG antibodies are transferred from mother to foetus through the placenta, or antivenom/antisera are administered after a snake bite. Passive immunity provides immediate but short-lived protection because the transferred antibodies are gradually broken down and no memory cells are formed.

questions.text_english:
(a) Study the flow chart given below. Name the hormones involved at each stage and explain their functions.
Hypothalamus → Pituitary → Ovary → Pregnancy
OR
(b) (i) Draw a diagram of L.S. of maize grain and label its any six parts.
(ii) Differentiate between perisperm and endosperm giving one example of each.

key_points: Hypothalamus → Pituitary: GnRH (Gonadotropin-releasing hormone) stimulates anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH.
Pituitary → Ovary: FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) stimulates follicle development and oestrogen production; LH (Luteinising Hormone) triggers ovulation and corpus luteum formation.
Ovary → Pregnancy: Oestrogen promotes endometrial proliferation; progesterone (from corpus luteum) maintains uterine lining for implantation and early pregnancy.

For OR (b)(ii): Perisperm is residual nucellus tissue persisting in seed — example: black pepper, beet. Endosperm is formed from triple fusion (3n) providing nutrition to embryo — example: coconut endosperm (liquid), wheat.

questions.image_description: Flow chart: Hypothalamus (releases GnRH) → Pituitary (releases FSH and LH) → Ovary (follicle development, ovulation, corpus luteum, secretes oestrogen and progesterone) → Pregnancy (progesterone maintains uterine lining). For OR: Longitudinal section diagram of maize grain showing pericarp, seed coat, scutellum, coleoptile, coleorhiza, plumule, radicle, endosperm.
questions.solution: At the Hypothalamus stage: The hypothalamus secretes Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH), which travels through the hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal system to the anterior pituitary and stimulates it to release gonadotropins. At the Pituitary stage: The anterior pituitary releases two hormones — FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone), which stimulates the growth and maturation of ovarian follicles and promotes secretion of oestrogen by follicle cells; and LH (Luteinising Hormone), which triggers ovulation (the release of a mature ovum) at the mid-cycle and then stimulates the remnant follicle to become the corpus luteum. At the Ovary stage: Oestrogen secreted by the developing follicle promotes proliferation and thickening of the endometrium. After ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, which further prepares and maintains the endometrium for implantation of the fertilised egg. At Pregnancy: Progesterone is essential for maintaining the uterine lining and supporting early pregnancy. Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) secreted by the developing placenta maintains the corpus luteum so progesterone secretion continues throughout pregnancy. (For OR option b: Perisperm is a nutritive tissue derived from the nucellus (maternal tissue) that persists in the mature seed. It is found in seeds of black pepper and beet. Endosperm is formed as a result of triple fusion — the secondary nucleus fuses with one male gamete to form the primary endosperm nucleus (3n), which develops into triploid endosperm. It stores nutrients for the embryo. Examples include coconut milk (liquid endosperm) and the starchy endosperm in wheat and maize.)
questions.solution_hindi: हाइपोथैलेमस → GnRH स्रावित करता है → अग्र पीयूष को FSH और LH स्रावित करने के लिए उत्तेजित करता है। FSH → पुटिका विकास और एस्ट्रोजन उत्पादन। LH → अंडोत्सर्ग और पीत पिंड निर्माण। एस्ट्रोजन → एंडोमेट्रियम की वृद्धि। प्रोजेस्टेरोन → गर्भाशय अस्तर का रखरखाव, गर्भावस्था का समर्थन। (OR: परिभ्रूणपोष = बीजांडकाय से बचा हुआ पोषी ऊतक, उदा. काली मिर्च। भ्रूणपोष = त्रिसंलयन से बना 3n ऊतक, उदा. नारियल।)

questions.text_english:
(a) Write the types and locations of the genes causing thalassemia in humans. State the cause and symptoms of the disease. How is sickle-cell anemia different from this disease?
OR
(b) (i) Enlist any four prime goals of the Human Genome Project (HGP).
(ii) List the two methodologies which were involved in the human genome project. Mention how they were used.
(iii) Expand 'YAC' and mention what it was used for.

key_points: Thalassemia genes: Alpha-thalassemia genes located on chromosome 16; Beta-thalassemia genes located on chromosome 11.
Cause: Mutations reduce or eliminate synthesis of alpha or beta globin chains of haemoglobin.
Symptoms: Severe anaemia, enlarged spleen, bone deformities, growth retardation.

Difference from sickle-cell anaemia: Sickle-cell is caused by a single point mutation in beta-globin gene (GAG→GTG, Glu→Val), producing abnormal HbS; thalassemia involves reduced/absent globin chain production (quantitative defect), not an abnormal haemoglobin structure.
For OR: HGP goals: sequence all 3 billion base pairs; identify all genes; store information in databases; develop tools for data analysis; address ethical issues.

questions.solution: Thalassemia is caused by mutations in genes coding for the globin chains of haemoglobin. Alpha-thalassemia is caused by mutations or deletions in genes located on chromosome 16, which code for the alpha globin chains. Beta-thalassemia is caused by mutations in genes on chromosome 11, which code for beta globin chains. The disease results from reduced or absent production of one of the globin chains, leading to imbalanced chain synthesis and destruction of red blood cells. Symptoms include severe anaemia requiring repeated blood transfusions, hepatosplenomegaly (enlarged liver and spleen), bone deformities due to compensatory expansion of bone marrow, and growth retardation. Sickle-cell anaemia differs from thalassemia in that it is caused by a specific point mutation in the beta-globin gene — adenine is replaced by thymine (GAG→GTG), changing the amino acid glutamic acid to valine at position 6 of the beta chain. This produces an abnormal haemoglobin (HbS) that polymerises under low oxygen conditions, making red blood cells sickle-shaped. Thalassemia is a quantitative disorder (reduced globin production), whereas sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative disorder (structurally abnormal haemoglobin). (For OR option b: Four prime goals of HGP were: to identify all approximately 20,000–25,000 genes in human DNA; to determine the sequences of all 3 billion chemical base pairs that make up human DNA; to store this information in databases; and to develop tools for data analysis and address ethical, legal, and social issues arising from the project. The two methodologies involved were: ESTs (Expressed Sequence Tags), which focused on identifying all expressed genes; and the Sequence Annotation approach, in which the total DNA from a cell was cloned in host organisms using vectors and then sequenced. YAC stands for Yeast Artificial Chromosome, which was used as a vector to clone large fragments of DNA for sequencing in the Human Genome Project.)

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) EcoR I has played a very important role in rDNA technology.
(I) Explain the convention for naming EcoR I.
(II) Write the recognition site of this endonuclease restriction enzyme.
(ii) Name the overhanging stretches of DNA produced by these restriction enzymes. Describe their role in the formation of rDNA.
OR
(b) (i) Insertional inactivation is a method to detect the recombinant DNA. Explain this method.
(ii) Name the commonly used vector for transferring genes in plants from bacteria.
(iii) How is this able to transform a normal plant cell into a tumour?

key_points: (a)(i)(I) EcoR I naming: E = Escherichia (genus); co = coli (species); R = RY13 (strain); I = first enzyme isolated from this strain.
(a)(i)(II) Recognition site of EcoR I: 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5'
(a)(ii) Sticky ends (cohesive ends) — single-stranded overhanging sequences; they allow foreign DNA and vector to join through complementary base pairing, then sealed by DNA ligase to form rDNA.

(b)(i) Insertional inactivation: foreign DNA inserted into antibiotic resistance gene of vector inactivates that gene; recombinants lose colour (white colonies) on X-gal plates while non-recombinants show blue colonies.
(b)(ii) Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens.
(b)(iii) Ti plasmid's T-DNA integrates into the plant cell genome, carrying genes for opine synthesis and phytohormone production, causing uncontrolled cell division — tumour (crown gall).

questions.solution: EcoR I naming convention: The name EcoR I is derived systematically — 'E' stands for Escherichia (the genus of the bacterium), 'co' for coli (the species), 'R' refers to the specific strain RY13 from which the enzyme was first isolated, and 'I' indicates it was the first restriction enzyme isolated from this strain. The recognition site of EcoR I is the palindromic sequence 5'-G↓AATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAA↑G-5'. EcoR I cuts between G and A on both strands, producing 4-nucleotide 5'-overhanging single-stranded ends. These overhanging sequences are called sticky ends (cohesive ends). In rDNA formation, when both the foreign DNA fragment and the vector are cut with the same restriction enzyme (EcoR I), both produce complementary sticky ends. These sticky ends allow the foreign DNA to anneal (join) with the linearised vector through complementary base pairing. The enzyme DNA ligase then seals the nicks in the sugar-phosphate backbone, creating a covalently joined circular recombinant DNA molecule. (For OR option b: Insertional inactivation is a technique used to screen for recombinant clones. In the vector pBR322, the lacZ gene encodes for beta-galactosidase. The foreign DNA is inserted into the lacZ gene, disrupting it. Non-recombinant bacteria (with intact lacZ) can cleave the substrate X-gal and produce blue colonies. Recombinant bacteria (with disrupted lacZ) cannot produce the enzyme and form white (colourless) colonies. Thus, white colonies indicate recombinant DNA. The vector commonly used for gene transfer from bacteria to plants is the Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens. The Ti plasmid contains a segment called T-DNA (tumour-inducing DNA) that can integrate into the chromosomes of the host plant cell. Once integrated, the T-DNA carries genes for synthesising special amino acids called opines and genes that produce phytohormones — specifically elevated levels of auxin and cytokinin — which cause uncontrolled and disorganised cell proliferation, transforming the normal plant cell into a crown gall tumour.)
questions.solution_hindi: EcoR I नामकरण: E = Escherichia, co = coli, R = RY13 (strain), I = पहला एंजाइम। पहचान स्थल: 5'-G↓AATTC-3'। स्टिकी एंड (cohesive ends) — एकसूत्री उभरे हुए सिरे जो vector और foreign DNA को पूरक क्षारक युग्मन से जोड़ते हैं; DNA ligase द्वारा सील होकर rDNA बनता है। (OR: insertional inactivation में lacZ जीन में foreign DNA डालने पर recombinant बैक्टीरिया सफेद colonies बनाते हैं; Ti plasmid का T-DNA पादप जीनोम में समेकित होकर हॉर्मोन जीन ले जाता है जो असामान्य कोशिका विभाजन और crown gall ट्यूमर बनाते हैं।)
